overview.summary: APPROVED (ADR-0001, 2026-09-28), NOT IMPLEMENTED: revision 8 Rust/Capy runtime with many described operations per file, declared and described outputs viewable from every surface (rivet outputs, GET /v1/operations/{id}/outputs, MCP rivet.outputs, Runtime::outputs), policy configured only by a policy.json file (absent file = deny-by-default for new application I/O), and one `rivet serve` listener that mounts HTTP, SSE, polling, WebSocket and MCP at once behind one authentication -> principal -> operation-authorization path. Revision 6 (UQ-18/R26) adds a generated I/O manifest: `rivet io` lists every effect site with its normalized target (URL, path, host:port, env var, connector method), fine-grained access verbs (read, list, stat, watch, create, update, append, delete, connect, bind, listen, exec, call, use, ...) and the policy capability that permits it, viewable by operation, target or capability, filterable by kind/access, rendered as table/json/markdown/csv, checked against policy.json (--check-policy) and turned into a least-privilege draft by `rivet policy generate`; policy.json grants and deny entries gain optional `access` narrowing. Revision 8 (TASK-005, approved by ADR-0001) adds option-derived file sites: every file-valued option line (tls ca_file/cert_file/key_file, http `body file`, operation-level descriptor) is its own allow_read site; every site carries origin (statement or option), phase (load|before_connect|connect|body|cleanup), requires_existing and secret; `rivet io --needs` lists, per operation, the files that must already exist before it can run, and `--check-files` stats them through the policy broker (exit 4 when one is missing, 3 when stat is not permitted); `policy generate` grants option-derived paths exactly with access [read]. Also covers full gRPC call modes, bounded sessions, OAuth 2.0, UDP and QUIC/HTTP3, Capy prefix-call syntax and a single error registry (code -> kind -> HTTP -> exit -> retryable). Approval gates G-DESIGN, G-CONTRACT and G-LIC are closed (ADR-0001; the maintainer owns Capy); the remaining entry gate for code is the Capy parser spike G-SPIKE (every S01-S159 example and docs/demos .rivet file parses cleanly). No runtime implementation exists. Companion draft sample bundles under docs/demos/ illustrate the contract; they do not implement or approve the runtime.

todos.todo: Hand each bundled source to the Parser port; the capy_parser adapter calls only Capy's public Library::parse and converts the ParseResult into Rivet's own SyntaxTree (domain::ast access is confined to infra/capy_parser.rs), keeping line/column spans (no byte offsets). If any diagnostic or recovered error region exists, return every syntax diagnostic (kind syntax, exit 2) and lower nothing. The grammar is Capy prefix calls: (request "id" {k: v}), (request.stream "id" {...}), named arguments as a trailing object, `x = (f a b)` and `node n after [a, b] = (request ...)`; durations are quoted strings matching ^[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h)$; ${...} holds dotted paths only; string escapes are limited to \n \t \" \\ \xNN \uNNNN.

Resolve operation IDs, types, lexical ownership and DAG edges without executing anything. Enforce header order (name, description, private, param*, output(+block), emits, receives, error*) and the leading-options rule: an option line after the first body statement of an operation or of a with/http/grpc block is syntax.option_after_body. Reject duplicate IDs, unknown options, DAG cycles, escaping handles, `while` without a finite enclosing deadline, and `return` used to produce a map/poll value (those bodies must `yield`). Detect static call cycles over literal (request "id" ...) targets (check.call_cycle). Warn when a `return` reads node.result without a status guard. Lower URL interpolation as component-aware (path segment vs query value; never adds segments, ?, # or @) and bind every `secret ... from env ... for ORIGIN` to its origins. Compute direct and transitive effects, marking targets that depend on caller params as knowledge param_dependent.

Validate OAuth profiles, declared token stores, QUIC ALPN and stream ownership, UDP modes and HTTP version/fallback choices; include token refresh, credential storage, UDP binds and QUIC migration in the static effect graph.

Parse any number of top-level operation/pipeline declarations per source file; retain callable ID, optional display name, description and described parameter schema. Lower each operation's output/emits/receives declarations through compile_output_spec and attach the resulting OutputSpec (plus its declared errors) to the RegistryEntry. Reject duplicate IDs across the bundle atomically with both source spans (registry.duplicate_id, exit 2) and build one immutable catalog for every surface, including the built-ins rivet.list, rivet.describe, rivet.outputs, rivet.request and rivet.sessions.*. Validate reserved rivet.* IDs and private visibility. A `fail` with a code not declared by an `error` line is a check warning. With strict_docs, reject blank public operation/parameter descriptions, a missing output description on any public operation, a missing description on any output/emits/receives field, and undeclared fail codes. Validate gRPC descriptor methods and cardinality without reflection or protoc I/O.

Read the operation's `output` line. Scalar form (`output text|integer|number|boolean|bytes|json|list T` with optional `description "..."`) produces a ValueSpec with no fields. Structured form (`output object [description ...]` ... `end`) opens a block: collect each `field NAME TYPE [required|optional] [description ...]` line in order, recursing into nested `field NAME object ... end` blocks; `required` is the default. If no output line exists the output type is json (opaque) with no description.

Reject (kind syntax, exit 2) an unknown type, a duplicate field name at the same level, an object field without an `end`, `open true` outside an object block, or a `list` without an item type. Objects are closed (additionalProperties:false) unless the block contains `open true`.

Apply the same field-block lowering to `emits` and `receives` item schemas. Collect every `error "code" description "..."` header line into DeclaredError{code, description, source}; reject a duplicate code in one operation.

Build the JSON Schema for output, emits and receives from the ValueSpec tree (types map text->string, integer->integer, number->number, boolean->boolean, bytes->base64 string, json->{} with no structural check, list T->array of T, object->object with required[] from required fields) and return the OutputSpec{id, output, emits, receives, errors, json_schema}. Pure lowering: no ports, no I/O.
Read the immutable registry snapshot, filter by caller authorization, and return IDs, schemas, effect summaries and source spans without connecting to dependencies.
Mark unresolved imported targets and dynamic dispatch as unknown; never report an incomplete catalog as a complete I/O inventory.

Project the same authorized catalog into CLI list/describe (describe now includes an Output section with params, output and errors; `list --outputs` adds a one-line output summary column), HTTP operation descriptors, the Rust registry and MCP tools/list. MCP direct named tools are canonical (tools/call {name:"users.get"}); each tool's outputSchema is the Completion envelope whose result property is the declared output schema; rivet.request, rivet.list, rivet.describe, rivet.outputs and rivet.sessions.* are listed as built-in generic tools. Preserve names, descriptions, defaults, constraints and input/output stream schemas; private operations and built-in grant/token internals remain hidden.

If `all` is true select every public operation visible to the caller's principal; otherwise require `id`. An id that does not exist, is private, or is not authorized for the principal returns not_found (404, exit 4) without disclosing whether it exists. Passing both id and all=true, or neither, is validation (422, exit 2).
Read each selected RegistryEntry.output from the immutable compiled catalog through Registry.outputs; never re-parse sources, connect to dependencies or execute the operation.

Return OutputReport{operations:[{id, name, output{type, description, fields}, emits|null, receives|null, errors:[{code, description}], json_schema}]} ordered by id. The same report backs `rivet outputs ID` (human table: output type/description, one row per field with type, required/optional and description, then emits, receives, errors, using an em-dash for absent parts), `rivet outputs ID --json` and `--all`, GET /v1/operations/{id}/outputs, the MCP built-in tool rivet.outputs {id?, all?} and Runtime::outputs(id).

Resolve ID and snapshot, reject unauthorized operation and unknown or invalid input fields before injecting defaults. Derive the child deadline, carry parent_request_id for nested requests and accept/emit W3C traceparent on HTTP surfaces. Intersect host ceiling, loaded policy.json and any per-request restriction (callers can only narrow). Refuse before scheduling when nested depth exceeds limits.max_call_depth (limit.call_depth), when the host-wide limits.max_concurrent_requests budget (default 64, shared by nested calls and DAG nodes) is exhausted (429 limit), or when limits.max_buffered_bytes (default 256 MiB) cannot reserve the request's queues.
Drive the compiled plan through the injected driver; validate each data frame, await callback demand, and propagate cancellation without replaying emitted data.

Join the request scope through ScopeSupervisor (await child cancellation and bounded resource cleanup in reverse acquisition order). Validate the final result against the operation's declared OutputSpec via validate_output BEFORE building the Completion; on mismatch return kind output_invalid, code output.invalid (HTTP 500, exit 5) with effects preserved. Return exactly one completion or primary error with suppressed cleanup errors and committed-effect status.
Check request ownership and distinguish an unknown request from an already terminal request without exposing another principal's request.
Signal the shared cancellation tree through RequestControl and return an idempotent acknowledgement; completion remains pending until cleanup finishes.

Reject cycles, ambiguous side-effect ordering and invalid references; assign nodes deterministic identities, attach per-node deadlines and effect requirements, and default the failure policy to `fail fast` when the dag header omits it. Every node starts pending.

Move a node pending->ready when all dependencies succeeded, then ready->running while the dag `limit` and the host-wide limits.max_concurrent_requests budget allow. A node whose dependency failed or was blocked becomes blocked. Under fail fast, the first failure cancels running nodes (-> cancelled) and marks never-started nodes skipped; under the retaining policy independent branches continue. Join every child through ScopeSupervisor before returning.

Expose each node's value as the envelope {status, result, error}; `.result` of a non-succeeded node is null. Return DagCompletion{result, nodes:[{id, status, error?, started_at?, ended_at?}], effects} where status is one of succeeded, failed, blocked, skipped, cancelled.
If the declared output type is json (opaque, including the default when no output line exists), return valid=true without a structural check.

Otherwise walk the result against the OutputSpec: scalar type must match (integer accepts only whole numbers; bytes must be base64); every required field must be present and non-null; optional fields may be absent; a closed object rejects any extra key; `list T` checks every element; nested objects recurse. Collect each violation as {path, expected, actual} (at most 32, then truncate with a count).

Return OutputVerdict{valid, violations}. When invalid also build RivetError{kind output_invalid, code output.invalid, retryable false, effects copied from the check input so committed effects stay reported}. Pure: no ports, no I/O, never mutates the result.
Validate create/read/update/delete mode, size bounds and version guards; request authorization for each source, destination and temporary path before opening handles.

Apply through FileAccess with directory-relative confinement; create exclusively, update only existing files with atomic replacement when supported, and delete only explicitly named entries. Refuse write/delete on a file whose link count is > 1 (file.hardlink_refused, permission 403/exit 3); treat Windows junctions/reparse points as symlinks; match selectors case-folded on case-insensitive volumes (default APFS, Windows) after Unicode NFC normalization. Preserve not_found, conflict and durability errors.
Resolve a pinned connector operation and schema; authorize logical tool/resource/prompt and transport independently; reject unsupported capabilities and schema changes.

Initialize or acquire the scoped MCP session, forward validated input with new correlation IDs, preserve content and structured results, and map protocol/tool errors distinctly; propagate cancellation and clean up owned sessions.

Resolve the entry set: explicit ids, else every public operation visible to the query principal (the default); `all` adds private helpers and operations unreachable from any public entry. An unknown or private id without `all` is not_found (exit 4) without disclosing existence. `transitive` defaults to true: follow literal (request "id" ...) edges (and connector imports) and record each site's call_chain from the entry (e.g. [data.snapshot, data.read]); each site appears once per entry that reaches it. Nothing is executed and no source expression is evaluated.

Ask Registry.effect_sites for the lowered effect sites of each selected operation from the immutable compiled catalog (never re-parse, never connect). One source line can yield several sites and each is kept: `file update` = stat + update, `with file open ... mode read` = read, an MCP stdio call = process exec + mcp call, an MCP/gRPC HTTP call = network connect + mcp/grpc call, an OAuth `auth` attachment = env read of the client secret + credential read/write + auth use + token-endpoint connect + resource connect. Retain branch conditions, source spans and secrets (with the origins they are bound to). Classify knowledge as exact | bounded | param_dependent | dynamic | opaque_remote | opaque_native; a connector's remote side effects are opaque_remote, a native host callback is opaque_native. With include_bootstrap, list the fixed runtime-internal sites separately under `bootstrap` (bundle + imports, policy.json, CA bundle, resolv.conf/system resolver, tzdata, descriptor/schema files, stdin/stdout/stderr) which are never granted to scripts. Every file-valued option line is its own site (kind file, access [read], capability allow_read): `tls ca_file`, `tls cert_file`, `tls key_file` in http/with http/with websocket/with quic/with tcp blocks and in grpc/mcp(http transport) connectors (a connector's option sites appear under every operation that calls it), `body file PATH` and `body multipart` `file NAME PATH` upload sources and an operation-level `descriptor PATH`. Connector-level `descriptor`/`schema` files stay bootstrap reads (never granted to scripts) but carry the same fields.

Map every site to its access verbs and capability with the fixed table: file read|list|stat|watch -> allow_read; file create|update|append -> allow_write; file delete -> allow_delete; network connect -> allow_network (plus `protocol` http1|http2|http3|ws|sse|grpc|quic|udp|tcp and, for HTTP, `method` GET/POST/...; a WebSocket upgrade is connect with protocol ws); network bind|listen|multicast_join -> allow_listen; process exec -> allow_exec; env read -> allow_env; pipe read|write -> allow_pipe; unix connect|listen -> allow_unix; mcp call (tool|resource|prompt) -> allow_mcp; grpc call (unary|server_stream|client_stream|bidi) -> allow_grpc; auth use|manage|status -> allow_auth; credential read|write -> allow_credentials. Source verbs map one-to-one: `file create` -> create (exclusive), `file update` -> stat + update, `file delete` -> delete, `file list` -> list, `file read` -> read.

Give every site origin, phase, requires_existing and secret. origin = SiteOrigin{statement} for the statement that produced it (file read, file create, http get, with tcp, grpc, secret, command, ...) or SiteOrigin{option} for an option line (tls ca_file, tls cert_file, tls key_file, body file, descriptor, schema, endpoint, transport command). phase = load (bundle load/assembly: descriptor/schema, operation-level descriptor) | before_connect (read to build a connection: tls files) | connect (open a connection or spawn a process: network/unix connect, process exec) | body (statements and body options: file statements, body file, env read by secret, mcp/grpc calls, send/receive) | cleanup (finally blocks and scope disposal). requires_existing (file sites only; false otherwise) = true when the file must already exist when the operation starts (read, stat, list, update's stat and update, delete without `missing ok`, every option-derived read); false when the site creates it (create, write, append), when a missing file is tolerated (`missing ok`), or when the same operation creates the same normalized target earlier in source order (e.g. `file create ./out/report.json` then `body file ./out/report.json`). A missing requires_existing file fails at that site with not_found (exit 4); for load/before_connect files that happens before the block dials, so the block causes no effect. secret = true when the content read is secret material (tls key_file, env read by a `secret` statement); the path is always shown, the content is never read by inspection and is redacted in traces.

Normalize each target into SiteTarget{template, scheme, host, port, path, glob, params} and a normalized display string: URLs as scheme://host:port with the default port made explicit (https 443, wss 443) plus a path/query template where interpolations become {param} (e.g. https://api.example.com/users/{id}); file paths relative to the bundle root with {param} for interpolated segments and, for param_dependent paths, the derived glob (./out/notes/*.json); UDP/QUIC as udp://host:port or quic://host:port; env vars as `env NAME`; connector methods as connector/kind/name (crm/tools/search, users/example.Users/GetUser); auth as profile/account; processes as argv[0] plus argv template. `params` lists the caller parameters the target depends on; a target computed from a runtime value (e.g. a received datagram's peer) is dynamic and has no glob.

Only when check_policy is set: build an EffectIntent (capability, access, method, protocol, target) for each reachable site and ask PolicyEvaluator.evaluate against the effective policy (host ceiling ∩ loaded policy.json, or deny-by-default when absent) without performing I/O. decision = allowed when a grant covers target and every access verb and no deny matches; denied when no grant covers it, a deny matches, or a grant's `access` list omits a used verb; partial when a param_dependent target's derived glob is only partly covered by grants; unknown when the target itself cannot be matched (dynamic, opaque_native). An opaque_remote site whose endpoint or connector method is exact is evaluated normally; only its server-side effects stay outside the manifest (and make complete=false). Record the policy file's path and sha256 in the manifest.

Only when trace_request_id is given: read that request's trace from TraceStore (same live host or configured persistent store; otherwise not_found exit 4) and join TraceEvent.effect_id to EffectSite.effect_id, filling attempts {count, last_decision, last_phase} so planned and actual effects appear side by side; trace rows with no matching site are appended as unplanned.

Filter by kind and by access (a site matches when any of its verbs is in the requested list; an access verb that does not belong to the requested kind is validation, exit 2). Build TargetSummary rows by grouping sites on (normalized target origin/path-or-glob, capability) with the union of access verbs, HTTP methods and operation ids (a transitive user is listed as `X (via Y)`); a group's decision is the worst of its sites (denied > partial > unknown > allowed). `by` = operation (default; one row per site ordered by operation id then source line, a transitive call shown as its own `(calls X)` row), target (TargetSummary rows) or capability (TargetSummary rows under allow_read / allow_write / ... headings); any other value is validation (exit 2). TargetSummary also carries origins, phases and needs_file (yes | no | `yes: <verbs>` for a mixed row | null for non-file rows); the by=target table columns are TARGET ACCESS CAPABILITY ORIGIN PHASE NEEDS FILE USED BY.

Only when needs (or check_files) is set: build IoManifest.needs as one OperationNeeds per selected operation listing its file sites with requires_existing true as NeededFile{path, effect_id, origin, phase, secret, knowledge, via, source, status:null}; include callee needs reached through literal (request ...) calls with via = the callee id; drop files the same operation creates earlier; show param_dependent paths as their template with knowledge param_dependent. Static: no I/O. Bootstrap load files (descriptor/schema) are listed only with include_bootstrap, under a separate bundle-load group, because loading the bundle already proves they exist. The table form prints `<operation> needs, before it can run:` followed by `path (origin[, secret])` rows, or `<operation> needs no existing files.`; json returns the IoManifest with needs filled. rivet.io takes needs?: boolean and HTTP GET /v1/io?needs=true; check_files is CLI/library only and is never a network parameter.

Only when check_files is set (implies needs; CLI --check-files or IoQuery.check_files): for every exact NeededFile ask FileProbe.stat(FileProbeInput{path, effect_id, context}); the file_access adapter first authorizes the probe through PolicyEvaluator as allow_read with access stat (a grant with no access list covers stat) against the effective policy (host ceiling ∩ policy.json) and only then performs a metadata probe plus readability check, never opening or reading content (key files stay unread). Set status = present | missing | unreadable (exists but the OS denies this process read access) | not_permitted (policy does not grant stat; the path is not touched) | not_checkable (param_dependent or dynamic path; not probed). Print each status beside its row and a stderr summary. Exit code: 3 when any file is not_permitted or unreadable (permission, checked first); else 4 (not_found) when any required file is missing; else the normal io exit code.

Return IoReport{manifest, by, format, rendered, exit_code} whose manifest is IoManifest{bundle{file,sha256}, policy{file,sha256}|null, complete, sites, targets, bootstrap} with complete=false when any site is dynamic, opaque_remote or opaque_native. Render the requested format from the same data: table (fixed columns OPERATION KIND ACCESS TARGET KNOWLEDGE SOURCE [DECISION] [ATTEMPTS], TARGET ACCESS CAPABILITY ORIGIN PHASE NEEDS FILE USED BY for by=target, TARGET ACCESS USED BY under capability headings for by=capability, and the per-operation needs listing for needs/check_files), json (the IoManifest itself; HTTP GET /v1/io, MCP rivet.io and rt.io always return this form), markdown (the same tables as Markdown) or csv (one row per site). IoManifest also carries needs (empty unless needs/check_files). csv adds origin, phase, requires_existing and secret columns (origin as `statement:file read` / `option:tls key_file`). Exit code: 3 when check_policy found any reachable site denied or partial, or check_files found a file not_permitted or unreadable; else 4 when check_files found a required file missing; else 7 when strict and complete=false (inspection incomplete; never probe a remote endpoint to complete static analysis); else 0. Serve exposure: over the network rivet.io is callable only by a principal whose serve.principals.<name>.operations lists it explicitly; loopback principal local may call it.
Authorize trace access and validate cursor and byte limits before reading the selected request trace.
Read sanitized ordered events through TraceStore, preserving request, parent, node, attempt, policy and source IDs; report gaps and incomplete traces instead of claiming tamper proof history.

Effective policy = host ceiling ∩ loaded policy.json (or the deny-by-default policy when no file was found) ∩ per-request restriction; HTTP/MCP/WS callers can only narrow, never grant. `deny` entries override `grants`. Guarantees cover script-initiated effects through brokered adapters only; the fixed bootstrap list is outside them and reported by io --include-bootstrap.

Validate capability and resolved target for every actual attempt including redirects, DNS results and file replacements. With network.deny_private_ranges (default true) refuse RFC1918, loopback, link-local, 169.254.169.254, fc00::/7 and fe80::/10 unless a grant names that IP/CIDR literally. Refuse secret use outside the origins bound by `secret ... for`. Reject unresolved or unsupported enforced boundaries before I/O; audit the allow or deny decision with policy_hash.

A grant matches an intent only when its capability and target selector match AND, if the grant carries `access`, every access verb of the intent is listed (absent `access` = every verb of that capability, the backwards-compatible default). A deny entry with `access` denies only those verbs; without it, the whole capability for that target. Example: allow_write ./out/** access [create] permits `file create` but denies `file update` (stat+update) with permission.denied (exit 3).

Require logical allow_auth/allow_credentials in addition to endpoint/storage permits; bind QUIC and UDP permits to protocol, destination and scope so QUIC internal UDP cannot authorize arbitrary raw UDP or a migrated peer.

If the caller passed --policy PATH (a path only, never grant text) use exactly that file; otherwise ask PolicyFileReader.discover for policy.json in the directory of the entry .rivet file. No environment variable is consulted. An explicit path that does not exist is config error policy.invalid (exit 2); an absent auto-discovered file is not an error.

When no file is found, return Policy{source absent, grants [], deny [], network.deny_private_ranges true, default limits (64 concurrent, depth 16, 256 MiB), serve none} so pure operations still run and every new application I/O is denied. There is no implicit allow-all; allow-all must be written as targets ["*"] and policy explain flags it as broad.

Read the bytes (PolicyFileReader.read, which also records sha256) and parse strict JSON. Require version == 1. Accept only the keys version, grants, deny, network, limits, serve, approved; any unknown key, unknown capability (allowed: allow_read ... allow_credentials), malformed selector, non-positive limit, serve.auth type other than none|bearer|mtls, bearer entry without a 64-hex sha256, or surface outside http|sse|poll|ws|mcp is policy.invalid (validation, exit 2) naming the JSON pointer. Library hosts reach the same validation through Policy::from_file(path) and Policy::from_json(bytes). Each grants/deny entry may carry an optional `access` array; every verb must belong to that entry's capability per the access table (allow_read: read, list, stat, watch; allow_write: create, update, append; allow_delete: delete; allow_network: connect; allow_listen: bind, listen, multicast_join; allow_exec: exec; allow_env: read; allow_pipe: read, write; allow_unix: connect, listen; allow_mcp and allow_grpc: call; allow_auth: use, manage, status; allow_credentials: read, write) — a verb from another capability (e.g. allow_write access ["delete"]), an empty array or a duplicate verb is policy.invalid (exit 2) naming the JSON pointer.

Resolve relative file targets against the policy file's own directory (not the cwd), normalise URL targets to scheme://host:port, and keep approved.snapshots / approved.overlaps sha256 lists: a schema snapshot or overlap acceptance counts as reviewed only when its hash is listed, otherwise program load fails.

Intersect the parsed grants with the host ceiling when a library host supplied one (a file can never widen it), compute policy_hash over the canonical JSON, and return the immutable Policy used by authorize_effect, start_serve and every request context.

Take the IoManifest built by inspect_effects for the requested ids (or all public operations). Drop bootstrap sites (never granted to scripts). Sites with knowledge exact, bounded or param_dependent are grantable; dynamic, opaque_remote and opaque_native sites go to `review` and are NOT granted.

Turn each grantable site into a (capability, target) pair: exact targets as written (./out/user.json, udp://127.0.0.1:7000, crm/tools/search, env name); param_dependent URLs collapse to their origin scheme://host:port; param_dependent paths become their derived glob (./out/notes/*.json); bounded targets use their bound set. File targets are written relative to the directory the draft will live in: the bundle root for stdout, or the --output file's own directory (policy targets always resolve against the policy file's directory). Option-derived file sites (origin.option: tls ca_file, tls cert_file, tls key_file, body file, operation-level descriptor) are always granted as their exact path with access [read] — never widened to a directory glob such as ./certs/**; a param_dependent option path is not granted and becomes a review item. Bootstrap descriptor/schema files are never granted.

Group pairs so there is exactly one grant per (capability, target), and set `access` to exactly the union of verbs the sites use, sorted in table order (e.g. allow_read [read, stat], allow_write [create]). allow_network grants carry no access list because connect is its only verb; methods and protocols are not policy selectors in v1.

Build PolicyFile{version 1, grants sorted by capability then target, network {deny_private_ranges: true}} with no deny, limits, serve, approved or secret material (serve auth and secrets are never generated). Validate the draft with the same schema rules as load_policy so it is guaranteed loadable. complete = review is empty.

Without an output path return the draft (CLI prints it to stdout; HTTP POST /v1/policy/generate, MCP rivet.policy.generate and Runtime::generate_policy return {policy, review, complete} and never write files). With --output ask PolicyDraftWriter.write_new, which creates the file exclusively and refuses an existing path with conflict.exists (exit 4) so a reviewed policy is never overwritten. List each review site on stderr (operation, kind, target, knowledge, source). Exit 7 when review is non-empty (the draft is still produced/written), else 0. The draft is a starting point for human review, not approval.

Resolve a configured OAuth profile and caller-owned account; reject unsupported grant types, unapproved redirect URIs, scope expansion and missing allow_auth or credential-store grants before creating transaction state.

Through OAuthSessionDriver mint bounded principal-bound state and PKCE S256 verifier for authorization code, or request a device code through an authorized endpoint; retain secrets in the transaction store and return only an expiring authorization URL or user-code challenge; never launch a browser implicitly.

Verify transaction ownership, expiry, configured issuer, exact redirect URI, single-use state and callback or device-poll mode; reject mismatch before token exchange and never log codes or device credentials.

Exchange authorization code with its PKCE verifier or poll the device token endpoint at the required interval under the request deadline. If wait:true reaches the request deadline while the provider still says pending, return {"state":"pending"} and do NOT consume the transaction; only explicit auth cancel or expiry invalidates it. On success persist rotated credentials atomically through the authorized store, consume transaction state, and return sanitized account status instead of tokens; preserve denial, expiry and uncertain exchange errors.
Bind profile and account to the authenticated principal and require status authority; reject cross-tenant identifiers without disclosing their existence.
Read only the authorized credential entry through OAuthSessionDriver and report connection state, granted scopes and expiry; do not refresh, discover endpoints or return token material.
Require ownership and disconnect authority for the account, cancel its active authorization transactions and prevent new credential leases from that generation.

Delete the local stored credentials and advance the account generation through OAuthSessionDriver; report local_only true because remote provider revocation is not implied, and refuse success if durable deletion fails.

rivet.auth.cancel {transaction_id}: resolve the transaction through OAuthSessionDriver and bind it to the authenticated principal that began it (principal-bound); a transaction owned by another principal, or an unknown id, is not_found (exit 4, HTTP 404) without disclosing that it exists. Requires allow_auth manage for the transaction's profile.

Invalidate the pending transaction through OAuthSessionDriver.cancel: discard its state, PKCE verifier and device code so a later rivet.auth.complete for it fails, stop any in-flight device poll owned by the calling request, and never contact the provider. Return AuthCancelReceipt{transaction_id, state:"cancelled"}.

Idempotent: cancelling an already-cancelled transaction returns the same receipt; a transaction that already reached a terminal state (connected, denied, expired) returns {transaction_id, state:<that terminal state>} unchanged and does not revoke stored credentials (use rivet.auth.disconnect for that). No token material, state or verifier appears in the receipt or the trace.

Require allow_auth use for the caller profile/account and verify resource origin, requested scopes, audience binding and active account generation; reject absent login instead of initiating an interactive flow.

Use a valid cached credential or serialize token acquisition/refresh by principal, account, profile, audience and scope set; authorize token endpoint and storage effects, respect expiry skew and refresh rotation, and return a scope-bound opaque lease only to the adapter; invalid_grant requires login and ambiguous refresh never blindly replays.

Validate peer, local bind, interface, datagram size and multicast options; require outbound network and any explicit listen grants before creating the socket, and treat implicit ephemeral client binds as part of the exact peer permit.

Drive bounded sends and receives through DatagramDriver; preserve datagram boundaries and sender metadata, reject truncation, do not infer delivery or replay lost messages, and close the scope on completion, timeout or cancellation; leave multicast groups during cleanup.

Validate QUIC v1, TLS identity, ALPN, stream and byte budgets, negotiated datagram requirement and disabled early data; authorize logical quic origin and its resolved UDP destination before handshake.

Open and join scoped bidirectional or unidirectional streams, apply explicit framing to reliable byte streams, propagate FIN versus reset separately, and reject unnegotiated or oversized datagrams; stream cancellation resets that stream without implicitly cancelling siblings.

Deny address migration unless explicitly enabled and newly permitted before probing or sending; aggregate connection and stream errors, await bounded cleanup in reverse ownership order, and never replay application writes on reconnect or transport fallback.

Resolve connector and fully qualified method against the pinned descriptor set; validate mode, input schema, metadata and message limits; require destination and allow_grpc grants before channel acquisition, and never perform implicit reflection or schema downloads.

Through GrpcDriver acquire a scoped verified HTTP/2 channel, bind optional authorized OAuth metadata, and exchange unary or streamed messages under deadlines and backpressure; input half-close signals completion without releasing the receive side.

Validate every response message and final gRPC status/trailers before success; preserve structured status and partial-output count on late failure, cancel only owned calls, and join scope cleanup without replaying unsafe mutations.

Resolve the caller-visible operation and parameter/input/output schemas; pin catalog version, principal, policy and deadline; enforce per-principal session and queue limits before scheduling any child effects.

Create a host-owned bounded child request scope and opaque principal-bound session ID through SessionDriver; return schema and sequence cursors without exposing handles; expire and cancel the scope on idle or total deadline.

Authorize session ownership and current operation access; reject completed input, wrong input schema, out-of-order send_seq or queue byte overflow before enqueue; a retry of the most recent sequence is accepted only for the identical payload hash.

Await queue capacity within the action deadline and enqueue through SessionDriver, then acknowledge local acceptance; never claim remote processing and never re-send an already acknowledged sequence to gRPC.
Authorize the live session and serialize with sends; reject unknown or expired sessions and preserve an idempotent already-finished response.

Mark input closed after already accepted messages, ask SessionDriver to deliver protocol half-close, and continue receiving output until terminal status or cancellation; this does not dispose the enclosing resource.

Authorize single-consumer access; validate after_seq against retained and previously delivered events, acknowledge only known delivered events, and reject future or expired cursors rather than pretending data exists.

Read up to max_events under bounded wait through SessionDriver, preserving event order and one terminal result/error; retain unacknowledged events for bounded replay, apply producer backpressure and report gaps explicitly.
Check principal and session ownership before accessing live state; treat repeated cancellation as idempotent while distinguishing unknown/expired state without cross-principal disclosure.

Signal the owned request cancellation tree through SessionDriver, stop input acceptance and await bounded protocol/resource cleanup; return a CancelReceipt carrying session_id and request_id; preserve committed effects and a final cancelled/error event for the retention period.

`rivet serve --stdio` serves MCP over stdio only (a stdio pipe cannot share a socket) and skips binding. Otherwise listen on --listen ADDR (default 127.0.0.1:8080). There are no --transport or --mcp flags.

Read serve.auth from the loaded policy (missing serve.auth = type none). If auth is none and the listen address is not loopback, refuse to start with serve.auth_required (exit 2) before binding anything.
Enabled surfaces = policy serve.surfaces or, when absent, all five: http, sse, poll, ws, mcp. A disabled surface's routes are not mounted and answer 404.

Bind once through ServeListener.bind, then mount each enabled surface on that one listener: http (POST /v1/request, GET /v1/operations, GET /v1/operations/{id}, GET /v1/operations/{id}/outputs), sse (POST /v1/request with Accept: text/event-stream), poll (POST /v1/requests, GET /v1/requests/{id}/events, POST /v1/requests/{id}/input|finish_input|cancel), ws (GET /v1/ws, subprotocol rivet.v1) and mcp (POST|GET|DELETE /mcp, Streamable HTTP). Every mount shares the same immutable catalog, dispatcher and broker and the same authenticate -> authorize path. If any mount fails, close the listener and return the error; never serve a partial surface set silently.

Return ServeReceipt{listen_addr, stdio, surfaces, auth_type, catalog_version, policy_hash}. With no policy.json serve still starts (loopback, auth none): pure operations work and all effects are denied.

Use the library host's Authenticator callback when one was supplied; otherwise the policy-driven adapter applies serve.auth. The same path runs for every surface: HTTP/SSE/poll requests, the WS upgrade request and each MCP HTTP request.
auth type none yields principal "local" only when the bound address is loopback (start_serve already refused otherwise).

auth type bearer: read `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`, sha256 it and compare in constant time against each configured tokens[].sha256; a match yields that entry's principal. Missing or unmatched token is kind auth (401) with no hint about which tokens exist; the raw token is never logged or traced.
auth type mtls: require a client certificate that chains to client_ca, then map its subject exactly to principals[].subject; no chain or no mapping is 401.
Private operations and unknown IDs are not_found (404) for every principal, so callers cannot probe for hidden operations.

If policy serve.principals is absent, every authenticated principal may call every public operation. If present, the principal must have an entry whose operations list matches the ID exactly or by a trailing `.*` prefix pattern (e.g. demo.* matches demo.add); no entry or no match is permission (403, exit 3).
Return AccessDecision{allowed, principal, matched_pattern}. Catalog listings (rivet.list, tools/list, GET /v1/operations, rivet.outputs --all) are filtered by the same decision. Pure: no ports.

Accept only JSON text frames on subprotocol rivet.v1 whose type is request, input, finish_input or cancel and which carry a client-chosen ref; malformed frames get {type:error, ref, error} with validation 422 semantics and do not close the socket.

type request: reject a ref already in flight (conflict) and a 9th concurrent ref (limit, max 8 per connection, same as sessions per principal). Authorize the operation for the connection's principal, then open a connection-owned child request through SessionDriver with a bounded 16-frame outbound queue.

type input {seq, data} -> SessionDriver.send with the same sequence rules as sessions.send; finish_input -> SessionDriver.finish_input; cancel -> SessionDriver.cancel. Frames for an unknown ref get an error frame.

Forward each emitted item as {type:data, ref, seq, data} via WsConnection.send, applying backpressure when the ref's queue is full; finish every ref with exactly one terminal frame: {type:result, ref, completion} or {type:error, ref, error}.
On socket close cancel and join every in-flight ref (connection-owned, unlike polling sessions, which survive reconnect). WS is a transport projection only: no WS-only operations.

POST /v1/requests {id, params} -> SessionDriver.open and return 202 SessionReceipt with events_url=/v1/requests/{session_id}/events. Unary operations may be submitted the same way as async jobs; their batch carries one terminal result event.
GET /v1/requests/{id}/events?after_seq=N&wait_ms=M -> SessionDriver.read (sessions.read) and return 200 SessionBatch; wait_ms is capped by the host maximum and returns early when events arrive.
POST /v1/requests/{id}/input -> SessionDriver.send; POST .../finish_input -> SessionDriver.finish_input; POST .../cancel -> SessionDriver.cancel returning a CancelReceipt that includes session_id.

Every route checks that the session belongs to the authenticated principal; another principal's or an expired session is 404. Sessions are principal-owned and survive client reconnects until idle/total expiry.

Build method, URL, headers and body from the lowered `http` block; URL interpolation was already encoded per component at compile time. Require the allow_network permit for scheme://host:port (and allow_auth / allow_credentials when an OAuth lease is attached) before any connection.

Send through HttpClient under the request deadline with the declared HTTP version/fallback; every redirect hop is re-authorized as a new target. Propagate W3C traceparent when the caller supplied one.

Decode the body through Codec per the block's `decode` option (json/text/bytes). A non-2xx status the operation does not map with catch/accept status becomes code http.status with details.status (kind http, exit 5, 502).
Require allow_network for ws(s)://host:port or tcp://host:port (plus allow_listen for any bind) before connecting; WebSocket performs the TLS/upgrade handshake, TCP connects raw or with TLS.
Exchange messages through SocketStream with explicit framing from Codec (WebSocket messages, or length-prefix/newline framing for TCP), bounded per-direction queues and deadline-counted flow control.
On completion, error or cancel: WebSocket sends a close handshake within grace, TCP half-closes then closes; the socket never outlives its lexical scope.
Require allow_exec naming the exact program path; argv is a list (no shell), environment starts empty and adds only allow_env-granted variables; cwd must be inside a granted directory.
Run through ProcessRunner with bounded stdout/stderr capture and the request deadline; stdin receives only declared input.

On deadline or cancel close stdin, terminate, then kill after grace and always reap; return exit status and captured output, mapping a non-zero exit to kind dependency (exit 5) unless the operation accepts it.

handling.role: Hand each bundled source to the Parser port; the capy_parser adapter calls only Capy's public Library::parse and converts the ParseResult into Rivet's own SyntaxTree (domain::ast access is confined to infra/capy_parser.rs), keeping line/column spans (no byte offsets). If any diagnostic or recovered error region exists, return every syntax diagnostic (kind syntax, exit 2) and lower nothing. The grammar is Capy prefix calls: (request "id" {k: v}), (request.stream "id" {...}), named arguments as a trailing object, `x = (f a b)` and `node n after [a, b] = (request ...)`; durations are quoted strings matching ^[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h)$; ${...} holds dotted paths only; string escapes are limited to \n \t \" \\ \xNN \uNNNN. Resolve operation IDs, types, lexical ownership and DAG edges without executing anything. Enforce header order (name, description, private, param*, output(+block), emits, receives, error*) and the leading-options rule: an option line after the first body statement of an operation or of a with/http/grpc block is syntax.option_after_body. Reject duplicate IDs, unknown options, DAG cycles, escaping handles, `while` without a finite enclosing deadline, and `return` used to produce a map/poll value (those bodies must `yield`). Detect static call cycles over literal (request "id" ...) targets (check.call_cycle). Warn when a `return` reads node.result without a status guard. Lower URL interpolation as component-aware (path segment vs query value; never adds segments, ?, # or @) and bind every `secret ... from env ... for ORIGIN` to its origins. Compute direct and transitive effects, marking targets that depend on caller params as knowledge param_dependent. Validate OAuth profiles, declared token stores, QUIC ALPN and stream ownership, UDP modes and HTTP version/fallback choices; include token refresh, credential storage, UDP binds and QUIC migration in the static effect graph. Parse any number of top-level operation/pipeline declarations per source file; retain callable ID, optional display name, description and described parameter schema. Lower each operation's output/emits/receives declarations through compile_output_spec and attach the resulting OutputSpec (plus its declared errors) to the RegistryEntry. Reject duplicate IDs across the bundle atomically with both source spans (registry.duplicate_id, exit 2) and build one immutable catalog for every surface, including the built-ins rivet.list, rivet.describe, rivet.outputs, rivet.request and rivet.sessions.*. Validate reserved rivet.* IDs and private visibility. A `fail` with a code not declared by an `error` line is a check warning. With strict_docs, reject blank public operation/parameter descriptions, a missing output description on any public operation, a missing description on any output/emits/receives field, and undeclared fail codes. Validate gRPC descriptor methods and cardinality without reflection or protoc I/O.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.

Read the operation's `output` line. Scalar form (`output text|integer|number|boolean|bytes|json|list T` with optional `description "..."`) produces a ValueSpec with no fields. Structured form (`output object [description ...]` ... `end`) opens a block: collect each `field NAME TYPE [required|optional] [description ...]` line in order, recursing into nested `field NAME object ... end` blocks; `required` is the default. If no output line exists the output type is json (opaque) with no description. Reject (kind syntax, exit 2) an unknown type, a duplicate field name at the same level, an object field without an `end`, `open true` outside an object block, or a `list` without an item type. Objects are closed (additionalProperties:false) unless the block contains `open true`. Apply the same field-block lowering to `emits` and `receives` item schemas. Collect every `error "code" description "..."` header line into DeclaredError{code, description, source}; reject a duplicate code in one operation. Build the JSON Schema for output, emits and receives from the ValueSpec tree (types map text->string, integer->integer, number->number, boolean->boolean, bytes->base64 string, json->{} with no structural check, list T->array of T, object->object with required[] from required fields) and return the OutputSpec{id, output, emits, receives, errors, json_schema}. Pure lowering: no ports, no I/O.

Read the immutable registry snapshot, filter by caller authorization, and return IDs, schemas, effect summaries and source spans without connecting to dependencies. Mark unresolved imported targets and dynamic dispatch as unknown; never report an incomplete catalog as a complete I/O inventory. Project the same authorized catalog into CLI list/describe (describe now includes an Output section with params, output and errors; `list --outputs` adds a one-line output summary column), HTTP operation descriptors, the Rust registry and MCP tools/list. MCP direct named tools are canonical (tools/call {name:"users.get"}); each tool's outputSchema is the Completion envelope whose result property is the declared output schema; rivet.request, rivet.list, rivet.describe, rivet.outputs, rivet.io, rivet.policy.generate and rivet.sessions.* are listed as built-in generic tools. Preserve names, descriptions, defaults, constraints and input/output stream schemas; private operations and built-in grant/token internals remain hidden.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.

If `all` is true select every public operation visible to the caller's principal; otherwise require `id`. An id that does not exist, is private, or is not authorized for the principal returns not_found (404, exit 4) without disclosing whether it exists. Passing both id and all=true, or neither, is validation (422, exit 2). Read each selected RegistryEntry.output from the immutable compiled catalog through Registry.outputs; never re-parse sources, connect to dependencies or execute the operation. Return OutputReport{operations:[{id, name, output{type, description, fields}, emits|null, receives|null, errors:[{code, description}], json_schema}]} ordered by id. The same report backs `rivet outputs ID` (human table: output type/description, one row per field with type, required/optional and description, then emits, receives, errors, using an em-dash for absent parts), `rivet outputs ID --json` and `--all`, GET /v1/operations/{id}/outputs, the MCP built-in tool rivet.outputs {id?, all?} and Runtime::outputs(id).
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.

Resolve ID and snapshot, reject unauthorized operation and unknown or invalid input fields before injecting defaults. Derive the child deadline, carry parent_request_id for nested requests and accept/emit W3C traceparent on HTTP surfaces. Intersect host ceiling, loaded policy.json and any per-request restriction (callers can only narrow). Refuse before scheduling when nested depth exceeds limits.max_call_depth (limit.call_depth), when the host-wide limits.max_concurrent_requests budget (default 64, shared by nested calls and DAG nodes) is exhausted (429 limit), or when limits.max_buffered_bytes (default 256 MiB) cannot reserve the request's queues. Drive the compiled plan through the injected driver; validate each data frame, await callback demand, and propagate cancellation without replaying emitted data. Join the request scope through ScopeSupervisor (await child cancellation and bounded resource cleanup in reverse acquisition order). Validate the final result against the operation's declared OutputSpec via validate_output BEFORE building the Completion; on mismatch return kind output_invalid, code output.invalid (HTTP 500, exit 5) with effects preserved. Return exactly one completion or primary error with suppressed cleanup errors and committed-effect status.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.

Check request ownership and distinguish an unknown request from an already terminal request without exposing another principal's request. Signal the shared cancellation tree through RequestControl and return an idempotent acknowledgement; completion remains pending until cleanup finishes.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.

Reject cycles, ambiguous side-effect ordering and invalid references; assign nodes deterministic identities, attach per-node deadlines and effect requirements, and default the failure policy to `fail fast` when the dag header omits it. Every node starts pending. Move a node pending->ready when all dependencies succeeded, then ready->running while the dag `limit` and the host-wide limits.max_concurrent_requests budget allow. A node whose dependency failed or was blocked becomes blocked. Under fail fast, the first failure cancels running nodes (-> cancelled) and marks never-started nodes skipped; under the retaining policy independent branches continue. Join every child through ScopeSupervisor before returning. Expose each node's value as the envelope {status, result, error}; `.result` of a non-succeeded node is null. Return DagCompletion{result, nodes:[{id, status, error?, started_at?, ended_at?}], effects} where status is one of succeeded, failed, blocked, skipped, cancelled.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.

If the declared output type is json (opaque, including the default when no output line exists), return valid=true without a structural check. Otherwise walk the result against the OutputSpec: scalar type must match (integer accepts only whole numbers; bytes must be base64); every required field must be present and non-null; optional fields may be absent; a closed object rejects any extra key; `list T` checks every element; nested objects recurse. Collect each violation as {path, expected, actual} (at most 32, then truncate with a count). Return OutputVerdict{valid, violations}. When invalid also build RivetError{kind output_invalid, code output.invalid, retryable false, effects copied from the check input so committed effects stay reported}. Pure: no ports, no I/O, never mutates the result.

Validate create/read/update/delete mode, size bounds and version guards; request authorization for each source, destination and temporary path before opening handles. Apply through FileAccess with directory-relative confinement; create exclusively, update only existing files with atomic replacement when supported, and delete only explicitly named entries. Refuse write/delete on a file whose link count is > 1 (file.hardlink_refused, permission 403/exit 3); treat Windows junctions/reparse points as symlinks; match selectors case-folded on case-insensitive volumes (default APFS, Windows) after Unicode NFC normalization. Preserve not_found, conflict and durability errors.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.

Resolve a pinned connector operation and schema; authorize logical tool/resource/prompt and transport independently; reject unsupported capabilities and schema changes. Initialize or acquire the scoped MCP session, forward validated input with new correlation IDs, preserve content and structured results, and map protocol/tool errors distinctly; propagate cancellation and clean up owned sessions.
Injected capability; no feature constructs adapters.

triggers.invocation: rivet --file <bundle> io [ID ...] [--all] [--transitive] [--include-bootstrap] [--by operation|target|capability] [--kind file|network|process|env|pipe|unix|mcp|grpc|auth|credential] [--access VERB[,VERB]] [--format table|json|markdown|csv] [--check-policy] [--strict] [--trace REQ] [--needs] [--check-files]
tools/call rivet.io {ids?, all?, by?, kind?, access?, check_policy?, needs?}

handling.role: Resolve the entry set: explicit ids, else every public operation visible to the query principal (the default); `all` adds private helpers and operations unreachable from any public entry. An unknown or private id without `all` is not_found (exit 4) without disclosing existence. `transitive` defaults to true: follow literal (request "id" ...) edges (and connector imports) and record each site's call_chain from the entry (e.g. [data.snapshot, data.read]); each site appears once per entry that reaches it. Nothing is executed and no source expression is evaluated. Ask Registry.effect_sites for the lowered effect sites of each selected operation from the immutable compiled catalog (never re-parse, never connect). One source line can yield several sites and each is kept: `file update` = stat + update, `with file open ... mode read` = read, an MCP stdio call = process exec + mcp call, an MCP/gRPC HTTP call = network connect + mcp/grpc call, an OAuth `auth` attachment = env read of the client secret + credential read/write + auth use + token-endpoint connect + resource connect. Retain branch conditions, source spans and secrets (with the origins they are bound to). Classify knowledge as exact | bounded | param_dependent | dynamic | opaque_remote | opaque_native; a connector's remote side effects are opaque_remote, a native host callback is opaque_native. With include_bootstrap, list the fixed runtime-internal sites separately under `bootstrap` (bundle + imports, policy.json, CA bundle, resolv.conf/system resolver, tzdata, descriptor/schema files, stdin/stdout/stderr) which are never granted to scripts. Every file-valued option line is its own site (kind file, access [read], capability allow_read): `tls ca_file`, `tls cert_file`, `tls key_file` in http/with http/with websocket/with quic/with tcp blocks and in grpc/mcp(http transport) connectors (a connector's option sites appear under every operation that calls it), `body file PATH` and `body multipart` `file NAME PATH` upload sources and an operation-level `descriptor PATH`. Connector-level `descriptor`/`schema` files stay bootstrap reads (never granted to scripts) but carry the same fields. Map every site to its access verbs and capability with the fixed table: file read|list|stat|watch -> allow_read; file create|update|append -> allow_write; file delete -> allow_delete; network connect -> allow_network (plus `protocol` http1|http2|http3|ws|sse|grpc|quic|udp|tcp and, for HTTP, `method` GET/POST/...; a WebSocket upgrade is connect with protocol ws); network bind|listen|multicast_join -> allow_listen; process exec -> allow_exec; env read -> allow_env; pipe read|write -> allow_pipe; unix connect|listen -> allow_unix; mcp call (tool|resource|prompt) -> allow_mcp; grpc call (unary|server_stream|client_stream|bidi) -> allow_grpc; auth use|manage|status -> allow_auth; credential read|write -> allow_credentials. Source verbs map one-to-one: `file create` -> create (exclusive), `file update` -> stat + update, `file delete` -> delete, `file list` -> list, `file read` -> read. Give every site origin, phase, requires_existing and secret. origin = SiteOrigin{statement} for the statement that produced it (file read, file create, http get, with tcp, grpc, secret, command, ...) or SiteOrigin{option} for an option line (tls ca_file, tls cert_file, tls key_file, body file, descriptor, schema, endpoint, transport command). phase = load (bundle load/assembly: descriptor/schema, operation-level descriptor) | before_connect (read to build a connection: tls files) | connect (open a connection or spawn a process: network/unix connect, process exec) | body (statements and body options: file statements, body file, env read by secret, mcp/grpc calls, send/receive) | cleanup (finally blocks and scope disposal). requires_existing (file sites only; false otherwise) = true when the file must already exist when the operation starts (read, stat, list, update's stat and update, delete without `missing ok`, every option-derived read); false when the site creates it (create, write, append), when a missing file is tolerated (`missing ok`), or when the same operation creates the same normalized target earlier in source order (e.g. `file create ./out/report.json` then `body file ./out/report.json`). A missing requires_existing file fails at that site with not_found (exit 4); for load/before_connect files that happens before the block dials, so the block causes no effect. secret = true when the content read is secret material (tls key_file, env read by a `secret` statement); the path is always shown, the content is never read by inspection and is redacted in traces. Normalize each target into SiteTarget{template, scheme, host, port, path, glob, params} and a normalized display string: URLs as scheme://host:port with the default port made explicit (https 443, wss 443) plus a path/query template where interpolations become {param} (e.g. https://api.example.com/users/{id}); file paths relative to the bundle root with {param} for interpolated segments and, for param_dependent paths, the derived glob (./out/notes/*.json); UDP/QUIC as udp://host:port or quic://host:port; env vars as `env NAME`; connector methods as connector/kind/name (crm/tools/search, users/example.Users/GetUser); auth as profile/account; processes as argv[0] plus argv template. `params` lists the caller parameters the target depends on; a target computed from a runtime value (e.g. a received datagram's peer) is dynamic and has no glob. Only when check_policy is set: build an EffectIntent (capability, access, method, protocol, target) for each reachable site and ask PolicyEvaluator.evaluate against the effective policy (host ceiling ∩ loaded policy.json, or deny-by-default when absent) without performing I/O. decision = allowed when a grant covers target and every access verb and no deny matches; denied when no grant covers it, a deny matches, or a grant's `access` list omits a used verb; partial when a param_dependent target's derived glob is only partly covered by grants; unknown when the target itself cannot be matched (dynamic, opaque_native). An opaque_remote site whose endpoint or connector method is exact is evaluated normally; only its server-side effects stay outside the manifest (and make complete=false). Record the policy file's path and sha256 in the manifest. Only when trace_request_id is given: read that request's trace from TraceStore (same live host or configured persistent store; otherwise not_found exit 4) and join TraceEvent.effect_id to EffectSite.effect_id, filling attempts {count, last_decision, last_phase} so planned and actual effects appear side by side; trace rows with no matching site are appended as unplanned. Filter by kind and by access (a site matches when any of its verbs is in the requested list; an access verb that does not belong to the requested kind is validation, exit 2). Build TargetSummary rows by grouping sites on (normalized target origin/path-or-glob, capability) with the union of access verbs, HTTP methods and operation ids (a transitive user is listed as `X (via Y)`); a group's decision is the worst of its sites (denied > partial > unknown > allowed). `by` = operation (default; one row per site ordered by operation id then source line, a transitive call shown as its own `(calls X)` row), target (TargetSummary rows) or capability (TargetSummary rows under allow_read / allow_write / ... headings); any other value is validation (exit 2). TargetSummary also carries origins, phases and needs_file (yes | no | `yes: <verbs>` for a mixed row | null for non-file rows); the by=target table columns are TARGET ACCESS CAPABILITY ORIGIN PHASE NEEDS FILE USED BY. Only when needs (or check_files) is set: build IoManifest.needs as one OperationNeeds per selected operation listing its file sites with requires_existing true as NeededFile{path, effect_id, origin, phase, secret, knowledge, via, source, status:null}; include callee needs reached through literal (request ...) calls with via = the callee id; drop files the same operation creates earlier; show param_dependent paths as their template with knowledge param_dependent. Static: no I/O. Bootstrap load files (descriptor/schema) are listed only with include_bootstrap, under a separate bundle-load group, because loading the bundle already proves they exist. The table form prints `<operation> needs, before it can run:` followed by `path (origin[, secret])` rows, or `<operation> needs no existing files.`; json returns the IoManifest with needs filled. rivet.io takes needs?: boolean and HTTP GET /v1/io?needs=true; check_files is CLI/library only and is never a network parameter. Only when check_files is set (implies needs; CLI --check-files or IoQuery.check_files): for every exact NeededFile ask FileProbe.stat(FileProbeInput{path, effect_id, context}); the file_access adapter first authorizes the probe through PolicyEvaluator as allow_read with access stat (a grant with no access list covers stat) against the effective policy (host ceiling ∩ policy.json) and only then performs a metadata probe plus readability check, never opening or reading content (key files stay unread). Set status = present | missing | unreadable (exists but the OS denies this process read access) | not_permitted (policy does not grant stat; the path is not touched) | not_checkable (param_dependent or dynamic path; not probed). Print each status beside its row and a stderr summary. Exit code: 3 when any file is not_permitted or unreadable (permission, checked first); else 4 (not_found) when any required file is missing; else the normal io exit code. Return IoReport{manifest, by, format, rendered, exit_code} whose manifest is IoManifest{bundle{file,sha256}, policy{file,sha256}|null, complete, sites, targets, bootstrap} with complete=false when any site is dynamic, opaque_remote or opaque_native. Render the requested format from the same data: table (fixed columns OPERATION KIND ACCESS TARGET KNOWLEDGE SOURCE [DECISION] [ATTEMPTS], TARGET ACCESS CAPABILITY ORIGIN PHASE NEEDS FILE USED BY for by=target, TARGET ACCESS USED BY under capability headings for by=capability, and the per-operation needs listing for needs/check_files), json (the IoManifest itself; HTTP GET /v1/io, MCP rivet.io and rt.io always return this form), markdown (the same tables as Markdown) or csv (one row per site). IoManifest also carries needs (empty unless needs/check_files). csv adds origin, phase, requires_existing and secret columns (origin as `statement:file read` / `option:tls key_file`). Exit code: 3 when check_policy found any reachable site denied or partial, or check_files found a file not_permitted or unreadable; else 4 when check_files found a required file missing; else 7 when strict and complete=false (inspection incomplete; never probe a remote endpoint to complete static analysis); else 0.
